app: Adversarial: occlusion & visibility tricks (the safety-claim stress test)
channel_setup: Naive distilled view vs a hardened in-page distiller (src/distill-hardened.mjs) with hit-testing; plus cross-window occlusion from the WM z-order map.

t1_read_text.detail: CSS visibility tricks handled correctly: opacity:0 and visibility:hidden secrets are NOT leaked into the view (filtered). Positive control.

t2_enumerate.detail: FOUND a silent-divergence class in the NAIVE view: a button covered by an overlay div was listed as present/actionable, but elementFromPoint at its center returns the overlay — a blind click would miss. Also found an off-viewport leak (content at left:-9999px appeared in the view with only a negative coord as tell).

t5_blind_action.detail: After hardening, the occluded button is emitted as '... [occluded]' so a router will NOT aim a blind click there; it falls back to scrolling/closing the overlay or to pixels. Failure is now explicit.

t6_pictorial.detail: Cross-window occlusion resolved geometrically: with two overlapping windows the router computes the back window as ~48% covered by the higher-z window from the WM map — so per-window content under the cover is knowably not-visible. Per-window structure alone is blind to this; the compositor map makes it explicit.

measurements.notes: Two genuine silent-divergence classes found and both closed: (1) in-window occlusion -> in-page hit-test marks [occluded]; (2) off-viewport leak -> dropped by viewport clipping; (3) cross-window occlusion -> resolved by WM z-order+geometry (back window 48% covered). Conclusion: NAIVE structure CAN be silently wrong about visibility/hittability; a safe channel must add a hit-test pass (within window) and use the compositor map (across windows). With those, no silent case survived. This is the key hardening result for the production-safety argument.

runtime_verification.method: elementFromPoint hit-test vs listed elements; rectangle-overlap vs z-order for cross-window
runtime_verification.agreement: post-hardening view matches what is actually visible & hittable; occluded/off-screen content is dropped or tagged, never silently asserted
